![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14195873/assets/38883c7cc4bfe8c9ecccadfcc2d0c75ff66f79b19ff697c15ddbe53f4c63dbab.png)

We need to create a cylindrical tin with a lid using $216\pi \,{cm}^{2}$ of sheet metal. What is the radius $r$ of the cylinder that has the largest volume?
question.worked_solution:
First, let $r$ be the radius and $h$ be the height of the cylinder.

We wish to maximize the volume

$$
V=\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

We know that the surface area is fixed at $216\pi \,{cm}^{2},$ so we also have the constraint equation

$$
2\pi rh+2\pi {r}^{2}=216\pi .
$$

Now, by making $h$ the subject of the constraint equation, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi rh & =216\pi -2\pi {r}^{2} \\ h & =\frac{216\pi -2\pi {r}^{2}}{2\pi r} \\ h & =\frac{108-{r}^{2}}{r}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the above into our expression for $V,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}V(r) & =\pi {r}^{2}\times \frac{108-{r}^{2}}{r} \\ V(r) & =(108r-{r}^{3})\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We want to maximize $V,$ so we need to differentiate $V$ and set the derivative equal to zero. The derivative is 

$$
{V}^{′}(r)=(108-3{r}^{2})\pi .
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives a stationary point, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(r) & =0 \\ (108-3{r}^{2})\pi  & =0 \\ 108 & =3{r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =36 \\ r & =6\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that, in the last step, we only considered the positive root because the radius $r$ must be positive.

Finally, we confirm that $r=6$ is a maximum using the second derivative test. The second derivative ${V}^{″}(r)$ is

$$
{V}^{″}(r)=-6\pi r,
$$

and we can see that ${V}^{″}(6)<0.$ So, the stationary point $r=6$ is indeed a maximum of $V(r).$

Therefore, the cylinder with the largest volume has a radius of $r=6\,\text{cm}.$
